_doc: Pressure catalog. Each operator is a forcing move. 'pool' names the seed pool its random seed comes from (a file in seeds/, or a dynamic pool: wall, killed, sparks, parts). 'needs' lists dynamic pools that must be non-empty for the operator to be usable. Templates use {seed}, {wall}, {spark}. Add operators by appending objects; no code change needed unless you add a new dynamic pool.

fresh.name: Collision
fresh.template: Build the idea so that its core mechanism IS this mechanism, transplanted into the problem: "{seed}". The borrowing is structural: a specific part of the seed becomes a specific part of the idea. If the idea would still make sense with the seed deleted, you failed.

fresh.name: Net removal
fresh.template: Everyone's obvious answer is "{wall}". It is now impossible, because: {seed}. Do not rescue or disguise the obvious answer. Solve what is left once that safety net is gone; the idea must work in a world where "{wall}" never existed.

fresh.name: Absurd constraint
fresh.template: Solve it under this non-negotiable constraint: {seed}. Do not cheat or soften the constraint; it must shape the core of the idea, not decorate it.

fresh.name: Inversion
fresh.template: Apply this inversion to the problem and build the idea from what the reversal reveals: {seed}.

fresh.name: Scale shift
fresh.template: Solve it at one extreme of this scale pair: {seed}. Pick the stranger end, make it genuinely work there, then bring back the one move that survives at ordinary size. The idea is that move.

fresh.name: Alien lens
fresh.template: Solve it the way {seed} would: use their actual working methods, tools and constraints, not their costume or vocabulary. If the idea only borrows their look or jargon, you failed.

fresh.name: Literalization
fresh.template: {seed}. Take this completely seriously, with no wink, and make the stupid version actually work for this problem.

fresh.name: Subtraction
fresh.template: {seed}. Remove it completely, even though it looks essential, and solve the problem without it. Do not sneak it back in under another name.

fresh.name: Brief mutation
fresh.template: Assume the brief is misstated. Restate the problem this way: {seed}. Then solve the restated problem. Begin the mechanism with the restated problem in a few words.

fresh.name: Wrong-answer excavation
fresh.template: This idea was rejected: "{seed}". Ask what would have to be true about the world, the people or the problem for it to be exactly right. Make that true, and build the idea that follows. Do not just repeat the rejected idea.

grow.name: Collide the spark
grow.template: Collide the spark with this mechanism: "{seed}". The new idea must keep the spark's connection but run on the seed's structure.

grow.name: Extremize the spark
grow.template: Push the spark to an absurd extreme along this scale: {seed}. Keep going past where it stops being sensible, then build the idea that lives there.

grow.name: Transplant the spark
grow.template: Transplant the spark to a different part of the problem: {seed}. Same connection, completely different location in the problem.

grow.name: Merge sparks
grow.template: Merge the spark with this other spark from a different idea: "{seed}". The child must need both; if either spark can be deleted, you failed.

grow.name: Invert the spark
grow.template: Invert the spark using this move: {seed}. Keep the connection, reverse its direction.

grow.name: Concretize the spark
grow.template: Give one concrete, physical embodiment that shares the spark but shares no surface with the parent: different objects, different setting, different people, different words.

parts: the very first moment someone meets the problem
the moment just after it fails
the person watching from the side, not the person doing it
the money: who pays and when
the physical object or place involved
the end, when someone stops or leaves
the waiting time nobody thinks about
the person who maintains it, not the one who uses it
the record or memory it leaves behind
the rules around it rather than the thing itself
the second time, not the first
the people who never show up
